one_liner: Small MIT C99 single-precision power-of-two FFT with runtime SSE/SSE3/AVX dispatch; 5-9x faster than KissFFT, near FFTW.
what_it_does: muFFT computes single-precision 1D and 2D FFTs (C2C, R2C and C2R) for power-of-two sizes and has a 1D fast-convolution API aimed at audio filtering, including interleaved-stereo-with-mono-filter. It uses an FFTW-like plan/execute/free interface (mufft_create_plan_1d_c2c, mufft_execute_plan_1d, mufft_free_plan_1d) on interleaved complex floats that are layout-compatible with C99 complex float and std::complex<float>. It is not source-compatible with FFTW or KissFFT, so call sites have to be ported.
how_it_is_fast: The Stockham autosort formulation removes the bit-reversal permutation pass. Hand-vectorised radix-2, radix-4 and radix-8 butterflies come in separate no-SIMD, SSE, SSE3 and AVX translation units, and the widest set the CPU supports is picked at runtime. Decompositions are chosen statically, so there is no FFTW-style measuring planner. Real transforms run as an N/2 complex FFT plus a final butterfly pass.
when_to_use: Single-precision power-of-two FFTs of moderate size (hundreds to a few thousand points) on x86-64 where FFTW's GPL is not acceptable
Block-based overlap-add FIR convolution for audio, including interleaved stereo signals and zero-padded inputs, via the built-in conv API
Replacing KissFFT on x86: in the gemmi shootout (i7-5600U, GCC 8 -O3) 1D C2C n=512 took 719 ns against KissFFT's 6553 ns, and the 2D 256x256 transform took 259 us against 1583 us
One portable binary that should use AVX where present and fall back to SSE or scalar code otherwise
when_not_to_use: Non-power-of-two sizes (n=384, 480 or primes): not supported; PocketFFT, pffft or FFTW cover them
Double precision or 3D transforms: not implemented
ARM/NEON targets: NEON was still listed as 'expected soon' when the last commit landed in 2019, so ARM gets the scalar path only
Peak 1D throughput: FFTW with a measured plan was faster at n=512 (588 vs 719 ns) on the same machine
Very large out-of-cache FFTs or tiny N=2/4/8 transforms: the README says neither is specially optimised

integration.dependencies: none for the library (libm); FFTW3f via pkg-config only for the optional bench/test binaries
integration.min_toolchain: C99; CMake 3.5+; GCC, Clang or MSVC
integration.platforms: any (scalar C); SIMD paths on x86/x86-64 only (SSE, SSE3, AVX)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Each plan owns a scratch buffer (tmp_buffer) that execute writes to, so one plan must not run concurrently on several threads; use a plan per thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different API from KissFFT (plan/execute with aligned buffers); data layout is compatible

gotchas: Input and output buffers must be SIMD-aligned (use mufft_alloc/mufft_calloc/mufft_free), and execute declares them restrict, so in-place transforms are not supported
Transforms are unnormalised, so forward followed by inverse scales by N; the convolution output, by contrast, is normalised
Do not build with -ffast-math: the CMake file warns that the code relies on -0.0f behaviour
The 2D R2C/C2R output uses a padded row stride for alignment, not the plain Nx/2+1 layout
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick muFFT over PFFFT when you need 2D transforms or an AVX path (pffft is SSE/NEON-only and was ~1.7x slower at n=512 C2C SIMD), or a ready-made convolution API. Pick PocketFFT for arbitrary lengths, double precision, 3D or ARM, and VkFFT for GPUs.
verified_claims_summary: The independent gemmi benchmark (public 1d.cpp/2d.cpp, GCC 8 -O3, i7-5600U, Ubuntu 18.04 FFTW packages, single precision) measured muFFT at 719 ns vs KissFFT 6553 ns for 1D C2C n=512, 4024 ns with SIMD disabled (1.6x like-for-like). In 2D 256x256 it took 259 us vs KissFFT 1583 us and FFTW measured-plan 306 us. 1D R2C n=512 took 511 ns vs FFTW meas. 681 ns and pffft 597 ns.
status_note: Abandoned since February 2019 (no NEON, no new sizes), but MIT-licensed, about 2.5 KLOC of C99 and easy to vendor; only the optional bench/test binaries fall under the GPL because they link FFTW.
